subject: Service degradation observed — SLA claim and postmortem request
messages:
From: Jenna Ruiz <jenna@acme.io>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>; acme-support@acme.io
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Service degradation observed — request SLA credit & postmortem

Hi Tessa,

We observed a sustained spike in error rates and latency against the Redwood inference endpoints used by our data-processing pipelines this morning. Our monitoring shows a clear degradation starting ~2026-02-15T16:07:00Z and lasting until ~2026-02-15T16:49:00Z (roughly 42 minutes). During that window we saw 502s and timeouts across batch inference jobs; downstream jobs retried and incurred backfill.

Can you confirm whether this was a Redwood infrastructure incident and whether Acme is eligible for SLA credit per section 4.2 of our agreement? We need:
- Formal confirmation of downtime window
- Incident ID (if available)
- Expected timeline for postmortem
- Instructions if we need to submit a claims form or PO for credit application

Attaching our internal request log and a sample stack trace. Please route to ops/SRE and let me know next steps. Our Finance team will want to reconcile any credits against PO ACME-3321.

Thanks,
Jenna Ruiz
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Analytics

Attachments: acme-sample-log-20260215.txt (text), acme-backfill-summary.csv (csv)

Subject: RE: Service degradation observed — request SLA credit & postmortem

Team — preliminary ops notes below.

We observed a scheduling regression in the serving pool that led to partially unavailable worker groups for a subset of model instances. Internal telemetry shows affected requests between 2026-02-15T16:06:30Z and 2026-02-15T16:48:55Z. Error spike and increased tail latency align with Acme's report. Incident created: INC-20260215-17.

Immediate actions taken:
- Restarted affected nodes and rolled forward a scheduler fix at 2026-02-15T16:50:10Z
- Enabled additional autoscale capacity for the impacted pool
- Collected KV cache and request traces for the window (attached: incident-logs-2026-02-15.zip)

Next steps:
- Ops will deliver a technical postmortem by EOD 2026-02-18 (target).
- Business ops (Rishi) to propose credit calculation consistent with contract 4.2.
- Triage to SRE runbook for permanent mitigation.

Based on the initial window, this looks like it meets the SLA disruption threshold for a credit. I'll attach the claims form scaffolded for Acme once we have your PO.

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-logs-2026-02-15.zip (log archive)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>; stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>; vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 10:20:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Service degradation observed — SLA credit calc (draft)

Quick draft for finance: per Acme's MSA (section 4.2 SLA credits), outage window ~42 minutes in a 30-day billing period corresponds to a service availability of 99.90% for the month (prelim). Contract tiers: 99.95%+ = no credit; <99.95% = sliding credit.

Our rough calculation gives an estimated credit of 10% of the monthly hosting fee for February, pending final verification by Finance and accounting for any overlapping scheduled maintenance. I've attached a working spreadsheet (SLA-credit-calculation.xlsx) with assumptions.

If Ops confirms the incident window and there are no offsets, we should be able to apply the credit either as a billing adjustment on the next invoice or via a dedicated credit memo, per Acme preference. Tessa — please confirm PO/finance contact and whether Acme prefers a credit memo or invoice adjustment.

Rishi
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA-credit-calculation.xlsx

- Eligibility: Ops and Revenue preliminarily confirm this meets the SLA credit criteria. Estimated credit: ~10% of February hosting charges (final amount subject to Finance verification).
